newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-TUIGAMALA BREAKS WORLD TRANSFER RECORD.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TUIGAMALA BREAKS WORLD TRANSFER RECORD.

text.p: Va'aiga Tuigamala became world rugby's first million-pound player on Wednesday when he turned his back on rugby league and Wigan to join Newcastle's all-star rugby union team.

The Western Samoan-born Tuigamala's transfer cost his new club 500,000 pounds ($808,000) but a five-year contract and compensation payments - Newcastle must repay his Super League loyalty bonus - elevates the deal to world record proportions.

Wigan allowed the former All Black winger to play union with Wasps in the current English winter, but have now sold him to the highest bidder to help ease their reported debts of over three million pounds ($4.9 million).
Newcastle are said to have doubled the 27-year-old Tuigamala's salary to add his powerful presence to a squad which already includes 13 internationals.

Newcastle chairman Sir John Hall, whose sporting empire also embraces Newcastle United Football Club as well as ice hockey and basketball franchises, hopes his new signing will have the same effect as Alan Shearer, who became the world's most expensive soccer player when he moved to the north-east for 15 million pounds ($24.3 million) last year.
"In the market-place you have to pay the going-rate and that's what we've done," said Hall. "The game has a tremendous future and we have to be there.
"It is my intention to establish the best sporting club in the world and the signing of Va'aiga Tuigamala is an indication of how serious an objective this is."
Tuigamala is ineligible for cup rugby so is likely to make his first appearance against Wakefield on March 8.
"The move to Newcastle has presented me with an opportunity I just couldn't turn down," he said. "It's an opportunity that enables me to return to the game I was brought up on."

Tuigamala spent three years at Wigan following his high-profile switch from union in January 1994. He won 19 caps for New Zealand before swapping codes, but played for Western Samoa in rugby league's World Cup in 1995 and represented them for the first time in a union test against Ireland last October.
The previous biggest transfer in rugby league involved last year's move to St Helens by British centre Paul Newlove, a 500,000 pounds ($808,000) deal which included a player-exchange.
Wigan chairman Jack Robinson commented: "He has given us three years magnificent service and obviously we're sorry to see him go. But this move will set him up financially for life."
